page: Microsoft Azure D64_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine deployed on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor based on x86_64 architecture, delivering 64 vCPUs across 32 dedicated physical cores with hyperthreading enabled at a base clock of 2.6 GHz. Cache provisioning features 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity sits at 256.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration includes instruction sets such as AVX-512F and AVX-512 VNNI, but lacks hardware GPUs and provides no bundled local disk storage, requiring remote storage solutions.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent, middle-tier throughput across standard computational routines. Stress-ng tests register single-core performance at 1,457.69 and multi-core output at 59,622.57, placing the instance within the average tier. Geekbench evaluations show a single-core score of 1,313.0 and a multi-core score of 11,865.0, paired with solid results in clang software compilation (35,492.0) and ray tracing (41,790.0). Memory throughput scales up to 175.21 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 69.18 GB/sec for uncached writes. Notably, the PassMark CPU extended instructions benchmark scored 55,022.71, ranking in the top 25% due to robust AVX-512 vector support.

The absence of dedicated GPU hardware exposes clear performance bottlenecks in autoregressive token generation. While small model prompt processing runs at 1,555.58 tokens per second, text generation drops into the bottom percentiles, achieving 40.31 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model and 6.87 tokens per second on a 7B model. Similarly, the lack of onboard NVMe storage necessitates reliance on network-attached storage, which can influence latency-sensitive I/O operations.

Microsoft Azure D64_v4 offers balanced cost efficiency for memory-heavy and multi-threaded enterprise workloads that require dedicated compute threads without the cost premium of dedicated accelerators. It is technically appropriate for enterprise software compilation, Redis in-memory caching (measured at 53.14 million SET operations per second), static web serving clusters, and relational database hosting dependent on remote managed block volumes.
description: Microsoft Azure D64_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. Featuring 64 vCPUs across 32 dedicated physical cores, the instance provides 256.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. The architecture includes AVX-512 instruction support, though it contains zero GPUs and provides no bundled local storage. In benchmark evaluations, the D64_v4 delivers mid-tier multi-core computing and memory throughput, highlighted by a strong PassMark extended instructions score of 55,022.71 and 53.14 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. However, text generation performance for language models is limited due to the lack of specialized accelerators. This configuration is best fitted for multi-threaded enterprise compilation, in-memory caching systems, data processing, and back-end application servers utilizing network-attached storage.
